abstract:
<jats:p>A hyperspectral scanning system was developed for three-dimensional (3D)
surface mapping in underground spaces, such as mine shafts and tunnels.
A hyperspectral line-scanning camera was mounted on the rotating driver
unit coaxial with the tunnel to image both the mine wall and the
ceiling. Uniform light was illuminated on the target surface to be
imaged using a halogen lamp rotating together with the hyperspectral
imaging sensor. A stereo camera, Light Detection and Ranging (LIDAR),
and Inertial Measuring Unit (IMU) were also attached to the sensor unit
together with the hyperspectral camera so that geometric information
could be acquired simultaneously during imaging. All sensor and
controller units were mounted on a cart-type platform for easy movement
in the tunnel, and a battery mounted on the platform supplied power for
system operation and the halogen light source. The developed scanning
system was tested in an actual mine, and 3D hyperspectral images of the
internal surface of the mine shaft were successfully obtained.</jats:p>
title: Development and Application of 3D Hyperspectral Scanning System for Underground Mine and Tunnel Exploration
